explain.say: Imagine taking a bus up a mountain in Ecuador or Colombia. In one day you pass banana farms, coffee bushes, potato fields and finally snow. Look at the board. The Andes are stacked in zones by height, and each zone grows different food.

explain.say: Start at the bottom: tierra caliente, which means hot land in Spanish, below about 1,000 metres. It is hot and steamy, perfect for bananas, cacao and sugar cane. Can you guess what happens to the temperature as we climb?

explain.say: It gets cooler! The air cools by about 6 degrees for every 1,000 metres you climb. In the tierra templada, the mild land, coffee grows on the slopes, like Colombia’s famous coffee. Higher, in the tierra fría, the cold land, farmers grow potatoes, and big cities like Quito and Bogotá sit there. Can you find the coffee zone?

explain.say: At the top, above about 4,500 metres, is the snowy zone, tierra nevada, with ice all year even near the Equator. Wonderful climbing! Wow fact: the top of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on Earth farthest from its centre, because the Earth bulges at the Equator.

faq.q: What are the altitude zones of the Andes?
faq.a: From low to high: tierra caliente, hot, below about 1,000 m; tierra templada, mild; tierra fría, cold; the high grasslands called páramo or puna; and tierra nevada, snow and ice. The exact heights vary from place to place.
asks: What grows at different heights in the Andes?

faq.q: Why is it colder higher up a mountain?
faq.a: As air rises it spreads out and cools, and higher up there is less air to hold heat. On average the temperature drops about 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m you climb, so high peaks stay snowy even at the Equator.
asks: Why is there snow on mountains near the Equator?

faq.q: Why are potatoes grown high in the Andes?
faq.a: Potatoes were first farmed in the Andes thousands of years ago and like cool weather. Andean farmers grow thousands of kinds and even freeze-dry them in the cold nights to make chuño, which keeps for years.

faq.q: Why do llamas live high in the Andes?
faq.a: Llamas and alpacas have thick wool, blood that carries oxygen well in thin mountain air, and they can live on tough grass. People use them for wool, carrying loads and meat.
asks: What is the difference between a llama and an alpaca?

faq.q: Why does coffee grow on mountain slopes?
faq.a: Arabica coffee likes warm, not hot, temperatures, steady rain and slopes that drain well. In the tropics these conditions are found part-way up mountains, like Colombia’s coffee region.

facts: On average, air temperature drops by about 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m of height.
Potatoes were first farmed in the Andes, in the region of southern Peru and north-western Bolivia.
The summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on Earth's surface farthest from Earth's centre.

quiz.say: Which crop grows best in the hot tierra caliente, low down?
quiz.show: In the hot tierra caliente, farmers grow…
quiz.why: Bananas need heat and humidity, found low down in the tierra caliente.

wrong.1: Potatoes like the cool tierra fría higher up.
wrong.2: Quinoa grows in the cool, high zones.

quiz.say: What happens to the temperature as you climb a mountain?
quiz.show: As you climb a mountain, the temperature…

options.show: Rises, because you are closer to the sun
options.say: Rises, because you are closer to the sun

quiz.why: Air cools as it rises and spreads out, so mountains get colder with height.

wrong.1: A few kilometres closer to the sun makes no real difference; thinner air matters more.
wrong.2: Temperature clearly changes with height; that is why peaks have snow.
